sources.what: Swiss job ads, public service of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs

sources.name: Federal Statistical Office (BFS), JOBSTAT
sources.what: Open positions by economic sector, quarterly

sources.name: Swiss Parliament (Curia Vista)
sources.what: Motions, questions and bills on asylum, status F and S, integration, skilled workers

sources.name: Eurostat, job vacancy statistics (Switzerland, information and communication)
sources.what: Job vacancies and the job vacancy rate in information and communication (NACE J) in Switzerland, quarterly, comparable across Europe.

sources.name: SECO, occupations under the job-reporting duty (Stellenmeldepflicht) 2026
sources.what: Official list of occupation groups where employers must report vacancies first to the job centres (unemployment of 5 percent or more); IT occupations are not on it, so IT ads are mostly voluntary.

sources.name: SEM asylum statistics: stock of persons in the asylum process (status N, S, F)
sources.what: How many people are in the asylum process or hold status N, S (temporary protection) or F (provisionally admitted), by canton and nationality; monthly.

sources.name: SEM asylum statistics: employment of persons with status F
sources.what: How many persons with status F (provisionally admitted) are of working age (18-64) and in work, by canton, nationality, sex and length of stay; monthly since 2025.

sources.name: SEM asylum statistics: employment of persons with status B
sources.what: How many persons with status B (recognised refugees with asylum) are of working age (18-64) and in work, by canton, nationality, sex and length of stay; monthly since 2025.

sources.name: SEM asylum statistics: employment of persons with status S
sources.what: How many persons with status S (temporary protection, e.g. from Ukraine) are of working age (18-64) and in work, by canton, nationality, sex and length of stay; monthly since 2025.

sources.name: SEM asylum statistics: employment of persons with status N
sources.what: How many persons with status N (asylum seekers) are of working age (18-64) and in work, by canton, nationality, sex and length of stay; monthly since 2025.

sources.name: BFS, resident population by residence permit
sources.what: Yearly count of people living in Switzerland by residence permit (B, C, Ci, L and the asylum permits F, N, S), for all of Switzerland.

sources.name: BFS, social assistance rate in the asylum sector (working age)
sources.what: Share of working-age (18-64) asylum seekers and provisionally admitted persons who receive social assistance, by canton, yearly. The lower, the more people are in work.

sources.name: SEM foreigner statistics (monthly Excel tables)
sources.what: Foreign resident population by permit, canton, nationality and age; immigration, emigration, naturalisation. Reference only: the numbers are in Excel tables 2-xx to 4-xx.

sources.name: SEM, working as a refugee or provisionally admitted person
sources.what: Rules for work permits and employer duties for persons with status F, B, S and N.

sources.name: SEM, Integration Agenda Switzerland
sources.what: Federal and cantonal goals for getting refugees into language, training and work, and the monitoring behind them.

sources.name: SEM, training situation of young provisionally admitted persons and refugees
sources.what: Report on how many young people with status F and B are in training or work.

sources.name: ESCO, European skills classification
sources.what: Official EU classification of skills; the dashboard links each skill to its ESCO definition where one exists.
